chunks: Hadith 2916 — And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Burayd al-ʿIjlī, who said:
I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who set out for hajj, and with him were his camel, expenses, and provisions, but he died on the way.

He عليه السلام said: “If he was a ṣarūrah and then died in the Haram, then the Hajj of Islam has sufficed for him. But if he died while being a ṣarūrah before entering into ihram, his camel, his provisions, his expenses, and what was with him are to be applied toward the Hajj of Islam. Then if anything remains from that, it belongs to the heirs, provided that he had no debt upon him.”
I said: “What do you think—if the hajj was voluntary, and then he died on the way before entering into ihram, to whom do his camel, his expenses, and what he had belong?”

He عليه السلام said: “All that he had with him and what he left behind belongs to the heirs, unless he had a debt, in which case it is paid on his behalf, or he had made a bequest, in which case that is carried out for the one to whom he made the bequest, and that is to be taken from one-third of his estate.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary area in which dying may count toward fulfillment of the obligation here
key_terms.ثُلُثِهِ: one-third of his estate, from which the bequest is executed
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj required once in a lifetime
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed by the deceased that must be settled
key_terms.صَرُورَةً: a person who has not yet performed the obligatory Hajj of Islam
key_terms.لِلْوَرَثَةِ: belonging to the legal heirs of the deceased
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or will made by the deceased
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to enter into the state of ihram for hajj

ai.seo_question: What happens if someone dies on the way to hajj before entering ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning a person who dies while traveling for hajj. It distinguishes between the obligatory Hajj of Islam and voluntary hajj, and explains how the deceased’s property is to be applied, including priority for debts, execution of bequests, and the rights of heirs.
